readings.source_reading: There are five arrows in the gutter strip on the inner margin of fol. 330. A short left-pointing arrow is at y≈1060, level with the second line of the 329b entry d. 1013(6). A long left-pointing arrow is at y≈1716, level with the 329b entry d. 989(4). A right-pointing arrow is at y≈2065, level with the 329b entry d. 998(1). A long left-pointing arrow is at y≈3490, level with the 329b entry d. 1013(5). A right-pointing arrow is at y≈3700, level with the 329b entry e. 240.
readings.evidence: In the native tiles, each arrow lies at the same height as an entry on the facing page. The left-pointing arrows point toward fol. 329b. The right-pointing arrows point toward entries on fol. 330. No connecting stroke to any specific entry is visible.
The third digit has an open, looped form. It could be a 4 or a 6. Other dates on the page do not settle the letterform.
The final cancelled digit has a long descending diagonal stroke below the line. This resembles a 7. It is partly obscured by the cancellation smudge.
A horizontal bar is visible over the A of the second 'Ali' in the native tile. The first 'Āli' also carries a macron but is overwritten.
The cursive reads approximately 'Raghuvaresalāsa'. The word ends in 'lāsa'. There is no 'taka' ending, so 'śataka' is not supported.
